docs.title: Overview
docs.text: gorestapi is a Go package that mounts a ready-made JSON REST API on top of a gocrud service. A single handler covers list, read, create, update, and delete for every route you register — with no code generation and no framework lock-in.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Define your structs and register them with a gocrud service.
  2. Configure one Route per URL path segment.
  3. Mount the handler on any http.ServeMux.
import (
    "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi"
    svccrud "github.com/mikogs/gocrud/pkg/service"
)

svc := svccrud.New(registry, db, gocrud.DialectPostgres)

handler := gorestapi.New(svc, gorestapi.Options{
    Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
        "notes": {},
    },
})

mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/api/", http.StripPrefix("/api", http.HandlerFunc(handler.Serve)))

Each registered route automatically exposes:

Method URL Operation GET /{path}/ List GET /{path}/{id} Read PUT /{path}/ Create PUT /{path}/{id} Update DELETE /{path}/{id} Delete

docs.title: Supported databases
docs.text:
gorestapi delegates all persistence to gocrud, which supports:

Database Driver PostgreSQL github.com/lib/pq SQLite modernc.org/sqlite

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/mikogs/gorestapi

docs.title: Demo
docs.text: See Demo for a complete runnable example covering two resources, ownership hooks, and server-side filters.

docs.title: Handler reference
docs.text: See Handler for the full Route, Options, and response format reference.

docs.title: Demo
docs.text: The cmd/poc directory contains a self-contained runnable server that demonstrates the most common gorestapi patterns: two resources related by a foreign key, ownership guards, and server-side filters. The walkthrough below follows that code.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
Two structs are defined — User and Note. A note belongs to a user through a foreign key. Users have numeric IDs, and notes have UUIDs, so that the URLs of notes do not reveal how many there are.

type User struct {
    ID         uint64
    Name       string `validate:"required,max=100"`
    Email      string `validate:"required,email" crud:"uniq"`
    CreatedAt  time.Time
    CreatedBy  uint64
    ModifiedAt time.Time
    ModifiedBy uint64
}

type Note struct {
    ID         string
    Title      string `validate:"required,max=200"`
    Content    string
    Comment    string
    UserID     uint64 `validate:"required" crud:"idx fk:user on_delete:cascade"`
    CreatedAt  time.Time
    CreatedBy  uint64
    ModifiedAt time.Time
    ModifiedBy uint64
}
  • The validate tags are checked on every create and update, and a failure is returned as 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.
  • crud:"uniq" makes the email unique. A second user with the same email is rejected with 409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION.
  • fk:user on_delete:cascade makes UserID reference a user. A note of a user that does not exist is rejected with 409 FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION, and deleting a user deletes their notes.
  • ID string makes gocrud generate a UUID for every new note, see The ID Field. The URL of a note is e.g. /api/notes/0190f5c3-6d1e-7b3a-9c4d-2e5f6a7b8c9d.
  • CreatedAt, CreatedBy, ModifiedAt and ModifiedBy are set by gocrud, from the time of the request and the user returned by UserIDFunc. Values sent by clients are ignored, and an update never changes CreatedAt and CreatedBy.

docs.title: Database and service
docs.text:
// SQLite checks foreign keys only when they are enabled for the connection
db, _ := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?_pragma=foreign_keys(1)")

svc := svccrud.New(map[string]func() interface{}{
    "users": func() interface{} { return &User{} },
    "notes": func() interface{} { return &Note{} },
}, db, gocrud.DialectSQLite)

svc.Migrate(context.Background())

Migrate creates the tables that do not exist yet, the user table before the note table that references it, and adds the columns of new fields to existing tables. The service registry maps URL path segments to their constructors. In production, keep the changes of the tables in migration files instead, see Versioned migrations.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Two hooks shape note behavior.

noteComment stamps every create and update with a server-controlled Comment field that clients cannot override:

noteComment := func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
    obj.(*Note).Comment = "Added with API"
    return nil
}

noteOwner rejects update and delete requests from users whose X-User-ID header does not match the note's stored UserID:

noteOwner := func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error {
    note := obj.(*Note)
    headerUserID, _ := strconv.ParseUint(r.Header.Get("X-User-ID"), 10, 64)
    if note.UserID != headerUserID {
        return errors.New("not the note owner")
    }
    return nil
}

AllowUpdate receives the stored record before the request body is applied, so noteOwner always checks the original owner rather than a value the client could forge.

docs.title: Handler
docs.text:
handler := gorestapi.New(svc, gorestapi.Options{
    UserIDFunc: func(r *http.Request) interface{} {
        id, _ := strconv.ParseUint(r.Header.Get("X-User-ID"), 10, 64)
        return id
    },
    Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
        "users": {},
        "notes": {
            AllowedFilters: []string{"UserID"},
            AllowUpdate:    noteOwner,
            AllowDelete:    noteOwner,
            PreCreate:      noteComment,
            PreUpdate:      noteComment,
            PostRead: func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
                obj.(*Note).Comment = "Returned from gocrud"
                return nil
            },
            PostListItem: func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
                obj.(*Note).Comment = "Returned from gocrud"
                return nil
            },
            FilterList: func(r *http.Request) gorestapi.FilterSet {
                return gorestapi.FilterSet{
                    Vals: map[string]string{"UserID": r.Header.Get("X-User-ID")},
                }
            },
            FilterRead: func(r *http.Request) gorestapi.FilterSet {
                return gorestapi.FilterSet{
                    Vals: map[string]string{"UserID": r.Header.Get("X-User-ID")},
                }
            },
        },
    },
})

FilterList and FilterRead automatically scope every notes query to the caller's user ID, so a user can only list and read their own notes. They are joined with AND around any client-supplied filter_val_* parameters, so a client cannot widen them.

docs.title: Mounting
docs.text:
mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/api/", http.StripPrefix("/api", http.HandlerFunc(handler.Serve)))
mux.HandleFunc("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    fmt.Fprintln(w, "ok")
})

http.ListenAndServe(":"+port, mux)

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
DB_PATH=poc.db PORT=8080 go run ./cmd/poc
Env var Default Description DB_PATH poc.db Path to the SQLite database file PORT 8080 Port the server listens on

docs.title: Trying it out
docs.text:
# Create a user
curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/users/ \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"Name":"Alice","Email":"alice@example.com"}' | jq

# Create a note owned by user 1, and keep its UUID
NOTE_ID=$(curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/notes/ \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-User-ID: 1' \
  -d '{"Title":"Hello","Content":"World","UserID":1}' | jq -r .data.id)

# List notes — only the caller's notes are returned
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/notes/ \
  -H 'X-User-ID: 1' | jq

# Read a single note (404 if UserID doesn't match)
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/notes/$NOTE_ID \
  -H 'X-User-ID: 1' | jq

# Update a note (403 if not the owner)
curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/notes/$NOTE_ID \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-User-ID: 1' \
  -d '{"Title":"Updated"}' | jq

# Delete a note (403 if not the owner)
curl -s -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/notes/$NOTE_ID \
  -H 'X-User-ID: 1' | jq
Request Behaviour GET /api/notes/ Returns only the caller's notes (UserID injected from header) GET /api/notes/{id} Returns 404 if the note's UserID does not match the header, or if id is not a UUID PUT /api/notes/ Creates a note with a new UUID, returned in data.id; Comment is stamped by PreCreate PUT /api/notes/{id} Updates a note; returns 403 if the caller is not the owner DELETE /api/notes/{id} Deletes a note; returns 403 if the caller is not the owner PUT /api/users/ with an invalid email Returns 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, with {"Email": "email"} in data PUT /api/users/ with an email of another user Returns 409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION PUT /api/notes/ with the UserID of a user that does not exist Returns 409 FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION DELETE /api/users/1 Deletes the user and, through the foreign key, their notes

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi"
    svccrud "github.com/mikogs/gocrud/pkg/service"
)

svc := svccrud.New(registry, dbConn, gocrud.DialectPostgres)

handler := gorestapi.New(svc, gorestapi.Options{})

New takes two arguments:

Argument Type Description svc *service.CRUD An initialised service instance options gorestapi.Options Configuration for the handler (zero value is valid)

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
type Options struct {
    CORS       cors.CORS
    Routes     map[string]Route
    UserIDFunc func(r *http.Request) interface{}
}
Field Type Description CORS cors.CORS CORS headers written on every response. Zero value emits no CORS headers. Routes map[string]Route Per-route configuration keyed by URL path segment. Only the paths in the map are served, other paths return 404. A route with the zero value has all operations enabled and all filters allowed, e.g. "notes": {}. UserIDFunc func(*http.Request) interface{} Called on every create and update request to obtain the current user's ID, passed to the service as ModifiedBy: a uint64, or a string for CreatedBy and ModifiedBy fields of type string, e.g. the subject of a JWT. When nil, or when it returns nil, ModifiedBy is 0 or "". When the struct has the CreatedAt, CreatedBy, ModifiedAt and ModifiedBy fields, gocrud sets them from this ID and the time of the request, ignores the values sent in the request body, and never changes CreatedAt and CreatedBy on an update.

docs.title: Route
docs.text:
Route maps a URL path segment to a service registry key and configures per-operation behavior.

type Route struct {
    RegistryKey    string
    Flags          int64
    AllowedFilters []string

    AllowCreate func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error
    AllowUpdate func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error
    AllowRead   func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error
    AllowDelete func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error

    PreCreate func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error
    PreUpdate func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error

    PostRead     func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error
    PostListItem func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error

    FilterList func(r *http.Request) FilterSet
    FilterRead func(r *http.Request) FilterSet

    CreateConstructor func() interface{}
    UpdateConstructor func() interface{}
    ReadConstructor   func() interface{}
    ListConstructor   func() interface{}
}

RegistryKey

When RegistryKey is empty the URL path segment is used as the service registry key. Set it explicitly when the URL path and the registry key should differ:

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "v1/users": {RegistryKey: "users"},
}

Flags

Flags is a bitmask that controls which operations and features are disabled for a route. Combine multiple flags with |. The zero value enables everything.

Constant Disables DisableCreate PUT /{path}/ (create) — responds 405 DisableUpdate PUT /{path}/{id} (update) — responds 405 DisableDelete DELETE /{path}/{id} — responds 405 DisableRead GET /{path}/{id} — responds 405 DisableList GET /{path}/ — responds 405 DisableFilters All filter_val_* / filter_op_* query parameters are ignored

AllowedFilters

AllowedFilters is a whitelist of field names that clients may pass as filters. When empty all fields are allowed (unless DisableFilters is set). Fields not in the list are silently dropped from the request, also in filter groups, e.g. filter_val_Status.q is allowed when Status is.

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {AllowedFilters: []string{"UserID", "Status"}},
}

Authorization hooks — Allow*

Each Allow* hook is called with the loaded object and the request. Return a non-nil error to reject the operation with 403 Forbidden.

Field When called Object passed AllowCreate After the request body is unmarshalled, before saving The new object populated from the request AllowUpdate After the existing record is loaded, before the request body is applied The stored record (original state) AllowRead After the record is loaded The loaded record AllowDelete After the record is loaded, before deletion The loaded record

AllowUpdate receives the record as stored in the database so it reflects the original owner or state — the incoming request values have not been applied yet.

noteOwner := func(obj interface{}, r *http.Request) error {
    note := obj.(*Note)
    headerUserID, _ := strconv.ParseUint(r.Header.Get("X-User-ID"), 10, 64)
    if note.UserID != headerUserID {
        return errors.New("not the note owner")
    }
    return nil
}

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {
        AllowUpdate: noteOwner,
        AllowDelete: noteOwner,
    },
}

Server-side filters — FilterList / FilterRead

These hooks add server-controlled filters to queries, e.g. that a record belongs to the signed-in user. They are joined with AND around all the filters of the client, so the client cannot get other records: a client filter on the same field only narrows the result, e.g. to nothing, and a filter group joined with OR stays inside them.

FilterList is applied to every list request (GET /{path}/), also with DisableFilters. FilterRead is applied when reading a single record by ID (GET /{path}/{id}); when set, the handler uses List(limit=1) with these filters and the ID, so mismatches return 404 rather than revealing record existence.

type FilterSet struct {
    Vals map[string]string // field → value
    Ops  map[string]string // field → operator (defaults to "eq" when absent)
}

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {
        FilterList: func(r *http.Request) gorestapi.FilterSet {
            return gorestapi.FilterSet{
                Vals: map[string]string{"UserID": r.Header.Get("X-User-ID")},
            }
        },
        FilterRead: func(r *http.Request) gorestapi.FilterSet {
            return gorestapi.FilterSet{
                Vals: map[string]string{"UserID": r.Header.Get("X-User-ID")},
            }
        },
    },
}

Pre hooks — PreCreate / PreUpdate

Called with the fully-prepared object just before it is written to the database. The request body has already been applied, and the ID is the one from the URL for an update, and 0 for a create. Use these to stamp server-controlled fields that should not be settable by the client.

Return a non-nil error to abort the operation with 500 Internal Server Error.

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {
        PreCreate: func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
            obj.(*Note).Status = "pending"
            return nil
        },
    },
}

Post hooks — PostRead / PostListItem

Called on loaded objects just before they are serialised to JSON. Use these to set or transform fields in the response that should differ from the stored values.

Field Fires on PostRead A single-record read (GET /{path}/{id}) PostListItem Each item in a list response (GET /{path}/)

Return a non-nil error to abort with 500 Internal Server Error. For PostListItem an error aborts the entire list response.

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {
        PostRead: func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
            obj.(*Note).Comment = "Returned from API"
            return nil
        },
        PostListItem: func(obj interface{}, _ *http.Request) error {
            obj.(*Note).Comment = "Returned from API"
            return nil
        },
    },
}

Constructor overrides

By default each operation uses the constructor registered for the key in the service. Setting a constructor here overrides that for the specific operation, allowing a different struct type — for example a create-only struct with fewer fields, so that clients cannot set the other fields when they create a record. The audit fields do not need it, as gocrud ignores the values sent for them.

Field Type Description CreateConstructor func() interface{} Constructor for PUT /{path}/ (create) UpdateConstructor func() interface{} Constructor for PUT /{path}/{id} (update). The existing record is loaded into this struct, and the request body is applied to it. ReadConstructor func() interface{} Constructor for GET /{path}/{id}. Only fields present on the override struct are SELECTed. ListConstructor func() interface{} Constructor for GET /{path}/. Only fields present on the override struct are SELECTed. 
// "_" suffix is stripped when deriving the table name:
//   strings.Split("Note_Draft", "_")[0] = "Note" → table "note"
type Note_Draft struct {
    ID      uint64
    Title   string `validate:"required,max=200"`
    Content string
    UserID  uint64 `validate:"required"`
}

Routes: map[string]gorestapi.Route{
    "notes": {
        CreateConstructor: func() interface{} { return &Note_Draft{} },
    },
}

docs.title: Mounting
docs.text:
handler.Serve is a standard http.HandlerFunc. Mount it under a prefix using http.StripPrefix so the handler only sees the path-relative URL:

mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/api/", http.StripPrefix("/api", http.HandlerFunc(handler.Serve)))
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)

After stripping the mount prefix the handler expects URLs of the form /{path}/{id} where path is a key from Options.Routes and id is an optional record ID: a number, or a UUID for structs with a string ID, see The ID Field.

docs.title: URL scheme
docs.text:
/{path}/           — list / create
/{path}/{id}       — read / update / delete

path must match a key in Options.Routes. id must be a single path segment of letters, digits, - and _, or absent, otherwise the response is 400 URL_PATH_ID.

An id that is not valid for the records of the route, e.g. abc for a numeric ID, or 42 for a UUID, is answered like an id that does not exist, with 404 NOT_FOUND, so that the response does not tell which IDs could exist. A UUID can be written in any letter case.

docs.title: Password fields
docs.text:
Fields tagged crud:"pass" are never included in responses from the Read and List endpoints. The handler strips them before serialising the object to JSON, regardless of whether the struct field has a json tag or not.

type User struct {
    ID       uint64
    Email    string `validate:"required,email"`
    Password string `crud:"pass"` // omitted from GET /users/ and GET /users/{id}
}

docs.title: List — GET /{path}/
docs.text:
Returns a paginated, filtered list of records.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description limit int 10 Maximum number of records to return offset int 0 Number of records to skip order string — Field name to sort by order_direction string — asc or desc, in any letter case filter_val_{Field} string — Filter value for the named field filter_op_{Field} string eq Filter operator for the named field: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge, like, match (PostgreSQL only), bit or in

Values are converted to the type of the field. For in, the values are separated with commas, e.g. filter_val_Status=paid,shipped&filter_op_Status=in. Times can be written as e.g. 2024-05-01 or 2024-05-01T10:30:00Z. For a nullable (pointer) field, an empty value is NULL: filter_val_ShippedAt=&filter_op_ShippedAt=eq lists the records without a value. See the gocrud service for the details.

Filter groups. The filters are joined with AND. To join filters with OR, put them in a group, by adding the same name of letters, digits or underscores after the field name and a dot, e.g. q in filter_val_Title.q and filter_op_Title.q. The filters of a group are joined with OR, and the group with AND with the other filters and groups.

Query Lists the records filter_val_Title.q=%25go%25&filter_op_Title.q=like&filter_val_Body.q=%25go%25&filter_op_Body.q=like with go in the title or the body filter_val_Status=paid&filter_val_Total.a=100&filter_op_Total.a=gt&filter_val_Express.a=true that are paid, and either cost more than 100 or are express filter_val_Total.min=100&filter_op_Total.min=ge&filter_val_Total.max=500&filter_op_Total.max=lt that cost from 100 to 500, as a group with one filter is joined with AND

%25 is the URL encoding of %, the wildcard of like.

An invalid filter is a 400 VALIDATION_FAILED response, with the failed rules in data, e.g. {"Status": "oneof"}.

Response 200 OK:

{
  "ok": true,
  "code": "SUCCESS",
  "data": [ { "ID": 1, "Title": "Hello", "..." : "..." } ]
}

When no records match, data is an empty list, [].

docs.title: Read — GET /{path}/{id}
docs.text:
Returns a single record by ID.

Response 200 OK:

{
  "ok": true,
  "code": "SUCCESS",
  "data": { "ID": 42, "Title": "Hello", "..." : "..." }
}

Response 404 Not Found:

{ "ok": true, "code": "NOT_FOUND" }

docs.title: Create — PUT /{path}/
docs.text:
Creates a new record. The request body must be a JSON object whose keys match the struct's field names (or json tags when set). An ID in the body is ignored, so a create cannot overwrite an existing record. The ID is assigned by the database, or a UUID is generated for a struct with a string ID, and returned in data.id.

Request body:

{ "Title": "Hello", "Content": "World" }

Response 201 Created:

{
  "ok": true,
  "code": "CREATED",
  "data": { "id": 42 }
}

For a struct with a string ID, id is the UUID, e.g. "0190f5c3-6d1e-7b3a-9c4d-2e5f6a7b8c9d".

Response 400 Bad Request (validation failure). data maps the fields that failed to the names of the failed validation rules:

{
  "ok": true,
  "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
  "message": "validation failed with violations: map[Email:email]",
  "data": { "Email": "email" }
}

Response 409 Conflict: UNIQUE_VIOLATION when a unique field already has the value, and FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION when the record references a record that does not exist.

docs.title: Update — PUT /{path}/{id}
docs.text:
Updates an existing record. The request body replaces the record's fields. Returns 404 if the record does not exist. The record is the one of the id in the URL: an ID in the body is ignored, so an update cannot write to another record.

Response 200 OK:

{ "ok": true, "code": "SUCCESS", "data": { "id": 42 } }

docs.title: Delete — DELETE /{path}/{id}
docs.text:
Deletes a record by ID.

Response 200 OK:

{ "ok": true, "code": "SUCCESS" }

Response 404 Not Found:

{ "ok": true, "code": "NOT_FOUND" }

Response 409 Conflict: FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION when other records reference the record with a foreign key that does not allow deleting it. Records referenced with on_delete:cascade are deleted along with it.

docs.title: Response format
docs.text:
Every response is a JSON object with the following shape:

{
  "ok":      true,
  "code":    "SUCCESS",
  "message": "optional human-readable detail",
  "data":    null
}
Field Type Description ok bool Always true — use code to distinguish outcomes code string Machine-readable result code (see below) message string? Present only on errors; contains a human-readable detail data any? Present on successful read / list / create / update, and on validation failures

Response codes:

Code HTTP status Meaning SUCCESS 200 Operation completed successfully CREATED 201 Record created NOT_FOUND 404 No record with the given ID VALIDATION_FAILED 400 Request body or a filter failed struct validation UNIQUE_VIOLATION 409 A unique field already has the value FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION 409 The record references a record that does not exist, or is referenced by other records BAD_REQUEST 400 Malformed URL, unparseable request body, or a method that is not supported for the URL, e.g. PATCH, or DELETE without an id URL_PATH_ID 400 The part of the URL after the route is not a single segment of letters, digits, - and _ NOT_ALLOWED 405 Operation is disabled for this route via Flags FORBIDDEN 403 An Allow* hook rejected the request SERVICE_ERROR 500 Internal error from the service or a Pre* / Post* hook

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
Populate Options.CORS to emit CORS headers on every response:

import (
    "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi"
    "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi/pkg/cors"
)

handler := gorestapi.New(svc, gorestapi.Options{
    CORS: cors.CORS{
        AllowOrigin:  "https://app.example.com",
        AllowHeaders: "Content-Type, Authorization",
        AllowMethods: "GET, PUT, DELETE",
        MaxAge:       3600,
    },
})

Each header is written only when its field is set. Set AllowCredentials: true to emit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Leave CORS as its zero value to emit no CORS headers. OPTIONS requests to any path are answered with 204 No Content and the CORS headers.

docs.title: JWT
docs.text: The pkg/jwt package provides RS256-based JSON Web Token issuance and verification, plus a JWKS endpoint helper. It wraps github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 for token operations and github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v3 for JWKS serialisation.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
NewProvider signs tokens with an RSA key, which you load from a secret. All the instances of an application, and the application after a restart, must use the same key: tokens signed with one key are rejected by a provider with another key.

Create the key once, e.g. with OpenSSL, and store it as a secret, e.g. in a secret manager, or in an environment variable of the deployment:

openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -out jwt-signing-key.pem

import pkgjwt "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi/pkg/jwt"

signingKey, err := pkgjwt.ParsePrivateKeyPEM([]byte(os.Getenv("JWT_SIGNING_KEY")))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("JWT_SIGNING_KEY: %v", err)
}

p, err := pkgjwt.NewProvider("https://auth.example.com", signingKey)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

func NewProvider(issuer string, signingKey *rsa.PrivateKey, options ...Option) (*Provider, error)
Argument Type Description issuer string The iss claim written into every issued token and validated on parse signingKey *rsa.PrivateKey The key that signs the tokens, of at least 2048 bits (pkgjwt.MinKeyBits) options ...Option WithTokenTTL and WithVerificationKeys, see below Option Description WithTokenTTL(ttl time.Duration) The time for which issued tokens are valid. Default: pkgjwt.DefaultTokenTTL, 1 hour WithVerificationKeys(keys ...*rsa.PublicKey) Keys that verify tokens, but do not sign them, e.g. the previous key after a rotation

The keys are loaded with:

Function Formats ParsePrivateKeyPEM(data []byte) (*rsa.PrivateKey, error) PKCS #8 (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, from openssl genpkey) and PKCS #1 (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY) ParsePublicKeyPEM(data []byte) (*rsa.PublicKey, error) PKIX (BEGIN PUBLIC KEY, from openssl pkey -pubout) and PKCS #1 (BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY)

Keys that are not RSA keys, or have fewer than 2048 bits, are rejected. In tests, pkgjwt.GenerateKey() returns a new key. Do not use it in an application: with a new key on every start, users are logged out by every restart, and the instances of the application reject the tokens of each other.

docs.title: Provider
docs.text:
type Provider struct { /* unexported */ }

func (p *Provider) Issuer()     string
func (p *Provider) PrivateKey() *rsa.PrivateKey
func (p *Provider) PublicKey()  *rsa.PublicKey
func (p *Provider) JWKS()       []byte
func (p *Provider) KeyID()      string
func (p *Provider) TokenTTL()   time.Duration
func (p *Provider) Issue(audience, subject, role string) (string, string, *time.Time, *time.Time, error)
func (p *Provider) Parse(rawToken, audience string) (*CustomClaims, bool)
Method Description Issuer() Returns the issuer string passed to NewProvider PrivateKey() Returns the signing key PublicKey() Returns the public key of the signing key JWKS() Returns the pre-built JWKS document, with the signing key and the verification keys, as JSON bytes KeyID() Returns the ID of the signing key, written as kid into the header of every token TokenTTL() Returns the time for which issued tokens are valid Issue(...) Signs and returns a new token (see below) Parse(...) Validates and parses a token (see below)

docs.title: Issuing tokens
docs.text:
signed, jti, issuedAt, expiresAt, err := p.Issue("myapp", "user:42", "admin")
Parameter Type Description audience string Written as the aud claim; must match what Parse expects subject string Written as the sub claim — typically a user ID or unique identifier role string Written as the role claim in CustomClaims

Returns:

Value Type Description signed string The compact-serialised JWT string, with the kid of the provider's key in its header jti string Unique token ID (UUID v4) — store this to support revocation issuedAt *time.Time Timestamp the token was created expiresAt *time.Time Timestamp the token expires, TokenTTL() after issuedAt

docs.title: Parsing and verifying tokens
docs.text:
claims, ok := p.Parse(rawToken, "myapp")
if !ok {
    // token is invalid, expired, or has wrong issuer/audience
}

subject := claims.Subject
role    := claims.Role

Parse validates the signature, expiry, issuer, and audience in one call. The signature is verified with the key of the kid in the header of the token: the signing key, or one of the verification keys. A token without a kid, or with the kid of another key, is rejected. It returns (nil, false) on any failure so callers never need to inspect a partial claims struct.

Parameter Type Description rawToken string Compact-serialised JWT from the request audience string Expected aud value

A clock skew tolerance of 30 seconds is applied automatically.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
type CustomClaims struct {
    Role string `json:"role"`
    jwt.RegisteredClaims
}

CustomClaims embeds the standard jwt.RegisteredClaims (which carries Subject, Issuer, Audience, ExpiresAt, IssuedAt, NotBefore, ID) and adds a Role field. Access standard fields directly via the embedded struct:

subject := claims.Subject   // whatever was passed to Issue
expiry  := claims.ExpiresAt // *jwt.NumericDate
role    := claims.Role      // "admin"

docs.title: Validating tokens from a remote issuer
docs.text:
When your service consumes tokens issued by a separate auth server, use ValidateWithJWKS. It fetches the JWKS document at the given URI, chooses the key that signed the token, and verifies the token — no local Provider needed.

The key is the one whose kid is the kid in the header of the token. This way, a JWKS can have several keys, e.g. while the issuer rotates them: tokens signed with the old key and tokens signed with the new key are both valid until the old key is removed from the JWKS. A token without a kid is accepted only when the JWKS has exactly one key, as there is no way to tell which key to use otherwise.

claims, err := pkgjwt.ValidateWithJWKS(
    ctx,
    "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json",
    "https://auth.example.com", // expected issuer
    "myapp",                    // expected audience
    bearerToken,
)
if err != nil {
    // fetch failed, key missing, or token invalid
}
Parameter Type Description ctx context.Context Controls the HTTP request to the JWKS endpoint jwksURI string Full URL of the JWKS document issuer string Expected iss claim value audience string Expected aud claim value bearerToken string The raw JWT string from the request

Returns a descriptive error if the JWKS cannot be fetched or decoded, if it has no keys, if it has no key with the kid of the token, if that key is not an RSA key, or if the token has no kid and the JWKS has more than one key. A token that fails signature, expiry, issuer, or audience validation returns the error invalid token.

docs.title: JWKS endpoint
docs.text:
Expose the public key to external verifiers (e.g. an API gateway or a frontend using a JWKS library):

http.HandleFunc("/.well-known/jwks.json", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    w.Write(p.JWKS())
})

The document is generated once by NewProvider and cached on the Provider. It has the signing key first, followed by the verification keys. To generate a JWKS from existing public keys directly:

jwksBytes, err := pkgjwt.JWKS(publicKey, previousPublicKey)

The kid of the key is its RFC 7638 thumbprint, a base64url-encoded SHA-256 hash of the public key, so the same key always gets the same kid. pkgjwt.KeyID(publicKey) returns it, e.g. to set the kid of tokens signed with the key by other code.

docs.title: Key rotation
docs.text:
Replace the signing key from time to time, or at once when it may have leaked. Tokens signed with the old key stay valid until they expire, when the old key is a verification key of the new provider:

  1. Create a new key, and keep the public key of the old one: bash openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -out jwt-signing-key-2.pem openssl pkey -in jwt-signing-key.pem -pubout -out jwt-previous-public-key.pem
  2. Deploy the application with the new key as JWT_SIGNING_KEY, and the old public key as JWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY: ```go var options []pkgjwt.Option if previous := os.Getenv("JWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY"); previous != "" { previousKey, err := pkgjwt.ParsePublicKeyPEM([]byte(previous)) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("JWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY: %v", err) } options = append(options, pkgjwt.WithVerificationKeys(previousKey)) }

p, err := pkgjwt.NewProvider("https://auth.example.com", signingKey, options...) `` New tokens are signed with the new key. Tokens of both keys are accepted byParse, and byValidateWithJWKSof other services, as the JWKS has both keys. 3. After the longest lifetime of a token,TokenTTL(), removeJWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY`. The tokens of the old key have expired by then.

When the old key leaked, skip the waiting: deploy the new key without JWT_PREVIOUS_PUBLIC_KEY, which logs out all the users, but also rejects the tokens that someone else signed with the old key.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "strings"
    "time"

    pkgjwt "github.com/mikogs/gorestapi/pkg/jwt"
)

const audience = "myapp"

func main() {
    signingKey, err := pkgjwt.ParsePrivateKeyPEM([]byte(os.Getenv("JWT_SIGNING_KEY")))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("JWT_SIGNING_KEY: %v", err)
    }

    p, err := pkgjwt.NewProvider("https://auth.example.com", signingKey, pkgjwt.WithTokenTTL(15*time.Minute))
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Issue a token for user 42.
    token, _, _, _, err := p.Issue(audience, "42", "member")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Println("token:", token)

    mux := http.NewServeMux()

    mux.HandleFunc("/.well-known/jwks.json", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
        w.Write(p.JWKS())
    })

    mux.HandleFunc("/protected", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        raw := strings.TrimPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
        claims, ok := p.Parse(raw, audience)
        if !ok {
            http.Error(w, "unauthorized", http.StatusUnauthorized)
            return
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello %s (role: %s)", claims.Subject, claims.Role)
    })

    http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)
}
